title: Interaction dropdowns permit and persist a degenerate self-interaction (same factor on both sides)
description: Dropdown 1 (l.413-421) lists ALL includedFeatures with no filter, while dropdown 2 (l.423-433) filters out only `factors[0]`. If the user picks factor A in dropdown 2 first (factors[1]=A) and then picks A in dropdown 1 (factors[0]=A), the config becomes `factors: ["A","A"]`. Nothing rejects or repairs this. Dropdown 2 then renders `value="A"` against an option list that no longer contains A, so the displayed selection is inconsistent with stored state.
evidence: l.420 renders every `includedFeatures.map(...)` for select-1 (no exclusion of factors[1]). l.430 select-2 does `includedFeatures.filter(f => f !== interaction.factors[0])`. updateInteractionFactor (l.185-193) writes the chosen value unconditionally with no equality guard. Resulting `["A","A"]` reaches backend _build_interactions (src/haute/modelling/_rustystats.py:77-97): len(factors)<2 is False so it is NOT skipped, and the per-factor loop builds a dict keyed by name (l.82-84) which collapses the duplicate to a single key `{"A": {...}, "include_main": False}` — a malformed one-term 'interaction'.
